title: Hold a property developer licence
what: Undertake the residential development activities the Act regulates only as a licensed property developer, licensed by the construction occupations registrar after an assessment of operational and financial capacity.

sources.title: Property Developers Act 2024 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 6(2)(a) (current republication (R9, from 1 October 2026; Property Developers Act 2024 | Acts))
sources.quote: establishing a licensing scheme that ensures certain residential development activities are only undertaken by licensed property developers

sources.title: Property Developers Act 2024 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 93(1) (current republication (R9, from 1 October 2026; Property Developers Act 2024 | Acts))
sources.quote: (a) the person makes a false or misleading representation that the person is authorised under a licence to undertake a residential development activity

sources.title: Property Developers Act 2024 (ACT)
sources.locator: sch 2 amdt 2.45 (Planning Act 2023 s 162A(2), inserted) (current republication (R9, from 1 October 2026; Property Developers Act 2024 | Acts))
sources.quote: The territory planning authority must not accept a development application in relation to the proposed residential building development unless— (a) the proponent for the development, or a related entity of the proponent, holds a property developer licence

sources.title: Property Developers Act 2024 (ACT)
sources.locator: dict, def registrar, words naming the body (found 23 Nov 2026) (current republication (R9, from 1 October 2026; Property Developers Act 2024 | Acts)
sources.quote: registrar means the construction occupations registrar.

reach.condition: if it undertakes residential development activities in the ACT (as the developer of regulated residential buildings)

confidence_note: Quoted from the register's current version, read on 23 Nov 2026. Section numbers read from the heading before each duty. The Act's objects and its offences about licences are quoted; the Act's amendment of the Planning Act 2023 (new s 162A) bars the planning authority from accepting a development application for a residential building development unless the proponent holds a property developer licence. Which activities are covered was not read.
